svg.title: Async-RBench: key evaluation mechanisms
svg.desc: The matched Linear and Async routes share participant-safe initial tasks and a benchmark-owned concurrent worker wave. Linear waits for all terminal child states before presenting one stable bundle. In Async, main and children execute concurrently. B completes before A, as shown by their common start and different bar endpoints. In the illustrated case only, Rule: A first requires gateway delivery of A before B may be released. The vertical control queue places teal A at the actual outgoing head nearest Main, with a continuous arrow from the top edge of A to the Main response boundary. Blue B is behind A with a pause marker and has no arrow to Main or A. Thus A visibly returns first while the already-completed B is held; the figure does not use a line from B to stand in for A presentation. There is no worker execution dependency. After A gateway delivery satisfies the configured prerequisite, B can be released, and its later actual main presentation respects the preceding active response-window boundary. No B presentation time is drawn. Gateway release itself need not await completion of main processing. This rule is one possible scenario policy among eight themes, not a universal ordering or all-results barrier; other policies can pass immediately, stage or replay notifications and generate supported runtime events. Maximum-action and deadline fallbacks remain applicable. The private Event rules panel uses a document with an edit mark for declared revise-artifact obligations and a document with a preservation shield for declared preserve-artifact obligations. These sets can be empty or inapplicable; they are not public instructions and do not require every event to cause replanning. Public submission validation is distinct from evaluator-private scoring. Private checks belongs to the common Scoring header and supports the separate BTS and DRS metrics. Equal theme weights is a shared Scoring footer applied independently to each metric, not an additional aggregate across metrics. Main can replan affected work and preserve other work together. Optional group Control means supported management rather than hot mutation of running child instructions. Actual presentation affects subsequent main execution without preempting an in-flight API call. All depicted execution extents are qualitative. Whole-run records independently support BTS and DRS; DRS combines half process and half event outcome without strict attribution to the displayed response segment. Each metric separately aggregates through repetitions and tasks to equal-weight event-theme means with coverage reported separately.
